x: Dave Carter performed well to finish 4th in the 220yds final, and Terry Newell and Dave Mitchell both qualified for the final of the 880yds; but nothing of note was produced. 1961 showed us a marked absence of "Claret and Gold".
In his heat Terry Newell showed little use of tactics and with 1:58.4 was sixth. However, it should be noted that this is his first season in trophy competition.

Gerry LeRoy opened with a win in the "A" 100 in 10secs and later added the 440, when he convincingly defeated Brian Morris (running for his second claim club) in 49.3. Terry Newell with a time of 51.7secs won the 'B' event. Alan Black was an easy winner of the mile.

With half a lap to go in the 880yds, defending champion John Davies looked an odds-on winner, but in the final straight first Terry Newell and then Dave Mitchell sprinted past, leaving a surprised John to finish fourth just behind Bhatia who had made up a tremendous amount of ground in the last 220yds.
In an Invitation Continental Relay we finished second to Polytechnic; our team of Leroy, Eldridge, Newell T., and Tolson recording 1:58.2 to Poly.'s 1:57.9.

After Terry Newell, Randy Glenn and Peter Pepe had run we were abreast of Blackheath, a good 15 yards clear of the remainder. Although he had run a half-mile heat and final during the afternoon, John Thresher took last stage.
Randy Glenn, Terry Newell and Alan Jackson produced a blanket finish for 2nd, 3rd and 4th, all recording 51.5. The hardest fought race of the day was the Senior 880 yards.
